hypotheses.name: Conductive alteration-front / radiometric edge co-orientation
hypotheses.signature_and_transform: At each scale, compute robustly standardized edge magnitude of log(1+cond_surf) and log-radiometric ratios; reward persistent co-oriented edges (axial cos(2*delta_angle) > 0) in a narrow corridor, with visible catalogue pixels exactly excluded. Freeze scale, signs, thresholds, and missingness handling before any fit.
hypotheses.blind_fault_rationale: A buried/poorly exposed permeable structure could focus fluids and clay alteration, perturbing electrical conductance and mobile/immobile radiometric ratios along a corridor that is not represented by the visible fault catalogue. This is a physical hypothesis, not evidence that the hidden labels share the pattern.
hypotheses.repo_distinction: The feature code contains separate conductivity gradients, radiometric ratios/edges, and radiometric-versus-DEM directional tests; the reviewed code/register does not contain this explicit conductance-edge × radiometric-edge orientation-coherence feature. Exact novelty outside this repository is unknown.
non_fault_mimics: alluvial clay or shallow soil moisture
airborne survey seams or resampling edges

hypotheses.name: Season-normalized Landsat surface-temperature lineament residual
hypotheses.signature_and_transform: For matched clear-sky seasonal observations, estimate a robust pixelwise surface-temperature residual after elevation, vegetation, illumination and seasonal baselines; test only persistent, spatially coherent lineaments and faults inferred from residual gradients. Aggregate to the competition grid only after cloud, emissivity and georegistration QA.
hypotheses.blind_fault_rationale: A permeable blind structure may channel warm fluids to the near-surface and produce a persistent thermal/vegetation response; this is indirect and may be absent where cover, depth or seasonal forcing dominates.
hypotheses.repo_distinction: The current repo uses airborne radiometry, magnetics, gravity, conductivity, DEM/LiDAR and sparse well/spring attributes; no multi-date satellite land-surface-temperature residual stack is implemented in the reviewed code.

hypotheses.name: Hydrothermal alteration mineral-boundary lineaments
layers: ASTER VNIR/SWIR surface-reflectance products where valid
hypotheses.signature_and_transform: Use only documented, QA-valid mineral-sensitive ratios or indices from suitable ASTER scenes; map persistent clay/iron alteration boundaries, then score line-like boundary coherence at 100 m after terrain, cloud, saturation and scene-date controls. Do not label vents or alteration pixels as fault truth.
hypotheses.blind_fault_rationale: A fault can focus hydrothermal fluids and alteration that forms a corridor or sharp alteration boundary even where the fault trace is buried; the hypothesized target remains fault pixels, not geothermal vents.
hypotheses.repo_distinction: No ASTER multispectral mineral-index time/scene stack is implemented. Existing airborne radiometric ratios and conductivity are not ASTER SWIR/VNIR mineral indices.

hypotheses.name: Persistent InSAR line-of-sight displacement discontinuities
layers: provided fault labels only for buffered hide-and-recover evaluation
hypotheses.signature_and_transform: After verifying acquisition geometry and coherent time-series coverage, estimate persistent line-of-sight velocity/displacement gradients and cross-trace discontinuities; require temporal and spatial consistency across independent interferograms, then aggregate to the 100 m grid.
hypotheses.blind_fault_rationale: Creep or repeated deformation localized on an unmapped structure can reveal a fault without using visible-catalogue geometry as a predictor. Inactive, deep, or poorly coherent structures may be invisible, so expected recall is limited.
hypotheses.repo_distinction: The current code uses coarse geodetic strain-rate and seismicity bands, not SAR interferometric phase/time-series products or pixelwise LOS discontinuities.
